messages:
emma (Support): Hey team, incoming from AcmeCorp — their users can't complete GitHub OAuth sign-in. Getting an error on the callback page: `invalid_request` and our logs show a state mismatch. Customer says it used to work and rolled no changes. Logged as SUP-4321 in the portal.

leo (Customer Success): Customer reported it started ~2 hours ago after they updated their CDN rules. Says the redirect_uri we return matches what they configured.

emma (Support): Repro steps from customer: 1) Click Sign in with GitHub on app 2) Complete GitHub auth 3) Redirect back to https://app.acme.example/auth/callback?code=...&state=... 4) App shows "Auth failed: state mismatch". They attached screenshots.

sahil (Eng Oncall): Copy of the relevant server log I pulled:

```
2026-03-14T15:12:03Z auth[pid=2124] INFO  oauth: begin auth request user=anon pkce=xyz123 state=abcDEF
2026-03-14T15:12:15Z auth[pid=2124] WARN  oauth: callback received user=anon state=Qv7t9 got=abcDEF error=state_mismatch
2026-03-14T15:12:15Z auth[pid=2124] ERROR oauth: aborting exchange: state mismatch - expected Qv7t9, got abcDEF
```

sahil (Eng Oncall): Looks like the state we expected (Qv7t9) doesn't match what comes back (abcDEF). Two likely causes: 1) our session cookie containing the stored state isn't sent back (cookie flags / SameSite), 2) redirect_uri changed during round-trip so GitHub redirects to a different host where the cookie isn't present.

mira (DevEx): Also check PKCE method — if the initial request uses `S256` and callback exchange expects `plain` we sometimes reject. But logs above point at state mismatch specifically.

emma (Support): Customer said they have a reverse proxy that strips query ordering and adds a trailing slash rewrite. Could that change `redirect_uri` canonicalization?

sahil (Eng Oncall): Yes. GitHub verifies `redirect_uri` against the OAuth app config exactly. If our app stored state keyed to a session cookie on `app.acme.example` but the callback arrives at `app.acme.example/` vs `app.acme.example` or with an added port, the cookie might not be included. Also if the CDN terminates TLS and rewrites headers, cookies with `SameSite=Strict` or missing `SameSite=None; Secure` can be dropped.

emma (Support): I asked for repro steps and they provided a curl of the callback URL they saw: `https://app.acme.example/auth/callback/?code=...&state=abcDEF` (note extra slash).

leo (Customer Success): Customer can reproduce consistently in Chrome but not in Firefox. They said incognito sometimes works.

mira (DevEx): Chrome recently tightened SameSite behavior. If we set session cookies with `SameSite=Lax` they might be omitted on cross-site POST/callback flows. OAuth callbacks are often cross-site because GitHub is the origin of the redirect. Solution: ensure session cookie for OAuth state uses `SameSite=None; Secure` so it is sent on the cross-site redirect.

sahil (Eng Oncall): Quick checklist for triage:
- Confirm the OAuth state is stored in a server-side session keyed from a cookie (we do that).
- Check Set-Cookie flags in initial response.
- Confirm callback request host exactly matches cookie domain.
- Verify the OAuth app `redirect_uri` in GitHub matches the final URL including trailing slash, port, and query path (must be exact).

emma (Support): I ran a quick capture against the customer's flow. When we initiate auth we set cookie: `Set-Cookie: session=ey...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` — there's the problem.

sahil (Eng Oncall): Changing to `SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly` should fix it for cross-site redirects. We'll need to roll a small patch and deploy. Pinged eng-runtime for quick patch and rollback plan.

oncall-bot: @sahil assigned SUP-4321 to eng-oncall, priority P1.

mira (DevEx): While we push the patch, customer workaround: 1) Use an incognito window or 2) temporarily use "Sign in with email" flow or 3) configure their CDN to preserve exact redirect URI and not add/remove trailing slash. I shared the docs page: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth#oauth-callback-issues

leo (Customer Success): Customer accepted incognito workaround and gave permission to proceed with a patch.

sahil (Eng Oncall): Patch plan: update auth middleware to set session cookie with `SameSite=None; Secure`, add a log that dumps `expected_state` from session and the `state` param on callback for debug (PII safe), and add a short e2e test that simulates a cross-site callback. Deploy to staging first.

emma (Support): Trial in staging confirmed state persisted after SameSite change. Staging log snippet:

```
2026-03-14T16:05:02Z auth[pid=2247] INFO oauth: begin auth pkce=S256 state=Qv7t9 set-cookie=SameSite=None
2026-03-14T16:05:12Z auth[pid=2247] INFO oauth: callback ok pkce=S256 expected=Qv7t9 got=Qv7t9
```

sahil (Eng Oncall): Deployed to prod with a canary on 10% of traffic. Monitoring: auth failure rate dropped from 6% -> 0.2% on canary hosts after the change. Rolling to 100% now.

emma (Support): Customer reported success after 20 minutes, confirmed users could log in normally.

leo (Customer Success): Customer asked for a root cause summary to send to their infra team. Drafted: "Root cause: session cookie used to store OAuth state had SameSite=Lax which made it omitted on GitHub's cross-site redirect in Chrome after their CDN rewrote the redirect URL (added trailing slash). This caused a state mismatch and auth failure. Fix: set cookie SameSite=None; Secure and recommend exact redirect_uri canonicalization on CDN."

mira (DevEx): Also adding note to our docs: emphasize exact `redirect_uri` matching (including trailing slash) and guidance to set cookies SameSite=None for OAuth flows. I'll open a docs PR.

customer-jira-bot: SUP-4321 status -> Resolved (root cause identified & fix rolled out).

emma (Support): Closing thread once we confirm the customer has no remaining issues — they acknowledged. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sahil (Eng Oncall): One more: we also validated PKCE uses `S256` everywhere for security — no mismatch there. Closing notes added to incident log. :white_check_mark:
